relationships.description: Connects Onion Architecture to system design hld architectures in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Placing pure domain entities and business invariants at the center so all framework, database, and UI dependencies point strictly inward.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Onion Architecture—from why N-tier database coupling rots codebases to enforcing inward ring boundaries in CI with ArchUnit.

spark.summary: An architectural style that places domain entities and business rules at the center, forcing all dependencies—frameworks, databases, and UI—to point strictly inward through interfaces.
spark.keyTakeaway: Isolate your core business logic from Spring, SQLAlchemy, or Kafka by defining repository and gateway interfaces inside the domain/application ring and implementing them in the outermost infrastructure ring.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Coined by Jeffrey Palermo in 2008, **Onion Architecture** places the **Domain Model** (entities, value objects, aggregates, domain events with zero ORM/HTTP annotations) at the center, surrounded by **Domain Services**.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Onion Architecture Inward Dependency Rule (UI/Web -> AppSvc -> DomSvc -> Infra -> Domain); PlaceOrder Execution Through Ports & Adapters (OrderController -> PlaceOrderUC -> Order Domain -> PostgresAdapter).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Onion, Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters), and Clean Architecture share the exact same Dependency Inversion core, differing mainly in ring naming. Explore how Onion Architecture pairs with Hexagonal Architecture, Domain-Driven Design, and Transactional Outbox.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore how Onion Architecture pairs with Hexagonal Architecture, Domain-Driven Design, and Transactional Outbox.

learningJourney.title: What is Onion Architecture
learningJourney.explanation:
Coined by Jeffrey Palermo in 2008, **Onion Architecture** places the **Domain Model** (entities, value objects, aggregates, domain events with zero ORM/HTTP annotations) at the center, surrounded by **Domain Services**, **Application Services** (use cases + output port interfaces like `OrderRepository` and `PaymentGateway`), and finally the outermost **Infrastructure & UI** ring (JPA, jOOQ, FastAPI, Kafka adapters).

The **Dependency Rule** is absolute: source-code imports may only point inward toward the center; inner rings never import outer-ring frameworks.

sectionDiagram.title: Onion Architecture Inward Dependency Rule
sectionDiagram.summary: Outer adapters implement interfaces defined in inner rings; the Domain Model imports only the language standard library.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Onion Architecture works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why we need Onion Architecture (and why N-tier couples to SQL)
learningJourney.explanation: In classic N-tier architectures, the database sits at the bottom of the dependency graph: business services import ORM entities and SQL clients directly. Upgrading Hibernate, swapping PostgreSQL for DynamoDB, or testing complex pricing rules forces you to boot a 6-second Spring context or mock SQL cursors. Inverting dependencies lets pure domain logic compile and run thousands of tests in under 15 ms with zero I/O.

ideas.title: Rich Domain Models Over Anemic Bags
ideas.description: Push invariant checks (`order.confirm()`, `wallet.debit(amount)`) onto domain aggregates instead of leaving entities as getter/setter DTOs with duplicated service validation.

ideas.title: CQRS Bypass for Complex Reads
ideas.description: Keep Onion aggregates for command/write paths, and allow slim read-only query projections that map SQL rows straight to response DTOs without N+1 aggregate loading.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Onion Architecture under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where Onion Architecture shines (and where it is overkill)
learningJourney.explanation: Apply Onion Architecture to long-lived, invariant-heavy domains; skip the mapping overhead for simple CRUD or analytics pipelines.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Billing Ledgers, Underwriting & Fulfillment
benefits: Protects complex state machines and regulatory rules from framework upgrades and vendor swaps (e.g., Stripe to Adyen).
costs: Adds explicit mappers between domain aggregates, JPA/ORM entities, and API DTOs (15–25% more files).

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Fast In-Memory Domain Unit Testing
benefits: In-memory repository fakes verify 80%+ of business rules in milliseconds without Docker/Testcontainers.
costs: Still requires contract/integration tests against real DBs to catch SQL unique-index and lock semantics.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Simple CRUD Services & dbt/Spark Pipelines
benefits: Direct table-to-JSON handlers or set-based SQL jobs ship faster without multi-ring mapping boilerplate.
costs: Forcing 4 rings onto a 2-endpoint CRUD service slows iteration for zero architectural benefit.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How Ring Boundaries are enforced in CI
learningJourney.explanation: Under deadline pressure, developers accidentally import `infra.postgres` or `@Entity` annotations into `domain/`. Prevent architectural drift automatically in CI using **ArchUnit** (Java/Kotlin) or **`import-linter`** (Python) so violating imports fail the build immediately.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```java
// ArchUnit CI rule enforcing Onion Architecture ring boundaries
Architectures.onionArchitecture()
  .domainModels("com.acme.orders.domain.model..")
  .domainServices("com.acme.orders.domain.service..")
  .applicationServices("com.acme.orders.application..")
  .adapter("persistence", "com.acme.orders.infra.postgres..")
  .adapter("rest", "com.acme.orders.infra.web..");
```
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Onion vs. N-Tier vs. Hexagonal vs. Clean Architecture
learningJourney.explanation: Onion, Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters), and Clean Architecture share the exact same Dependency Inversion core, differing mainly in ring naming.

benefits: Separates Domain Model from Domain Services and Application Services with explicit concentric rings.
costs: Requires discipline to avoid anemic domain models and heavy N+1 aggregate reads.

benefits: Symmetric inside/outside view—ideal when driving (REST/CLI) and driven (DB/Kafka) adapters are equally important.
costs: Less prescriptive about internal domain-vs-application layering.

benefits: Minimal boilerplate and familiar to any developer for simple CRUD apps.
costs: Transitively couples business logic to ORM entities, lazy-loading proxies, and SQL schemas.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production example: PlaceOrder Use Case Across Rings
learningJourney.explanation: At runtime, `OrderController` (Web adapter) deserializes `POST /orders` and calls `PlaceOrderUseCase` (Application ring). The use case loads pure `Order` aggregates via `OrderRepository` (Port implemented by Postgres adapter), executes `order.confirm()` in pure domain code, and persists via the adapter.

sectionDiagram.summary: Runtime calls flow outward-in-out, while compile-time imports point strictly inward toward Domain.

knowledgeCheck.question: In Onion Architecture, where should the `OrderRepository` interface live versus its PostgreSQL JPA implementation?

options.text: The interface lives in the inner Domain/Application ring; the JPA implementation lives in the outer Infrastructure ring
options.feedback: Correct: dependency inversion keeps inner rings independent of PostgreSQL or JPA.

options.text: Both the interface and JPA implementation live in the Domain Model ring
options.feedback: Placing JPA in the Domain Model violates the inward-only Dependency Rule.

options.text: The interface lives in the Infrastructure ring and is imported by the Domain Model
options.feedback: Inner rings must never import from outer rings.

beginner.byteSummary:
**The Core Idea (Beginner):** Coined by Jeffrey Palermo in 2008, **Onion Architecture** places the **Domain Model** (entities, value objects, aggregates, domain events with zero ORM/HTTP annotations) at the center, surrounded by **Domain Services**.

**How It Flows:** Think of Onion Architecture as a clear step-by-step chain: UI/Web -> AppSvc -> DomSvc -> Infra -> OrderController.

**Why Beginners Should Care:** Isolate your core business logic from Spring, SQLAlchemy, or Kafka by defining repository and gateway interfaces inside the domain/application ring and implementing them in the outermost infrastructure ring.

_recommendedProblem.title: Design a Double-Entry Payment & Ledger System
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Design a payment and ledger system (like Stripe or PayPal) processing 5,000 TPS where no dollar can ever be double-charged, lost, or created out of thin air—even across network retries and PSP timeouts.
